---
title: "NGS library preparation"
title-block-banner: false
---

Course materials for a course on **next-generation sequencing (NGS) library preparation**: how to turn a tube of DNA or RNA into something a sequencer can read, and how to tell whether you did it right.

Every exercise page has collapsible **Hint** and **Solution** callouts. Try first, then peek.

## Module 1 — Introduction to NGS

Sequencing platforms, what a "library" is, and the anatomy of a sequencing read.

- Lecture: [Introduction to NGS](module1/lectures/1_intro.html)
- Exercise: [Anatomy of a library molecule](module1/exercises/1_library_anatomy.html)

## Module 2 — Core library preparation workflow

Fragmentation, end repair, A-tailing, adapter ligation, PCR amplification and size selection.

- Lecture: [The core workflow](module2/lectures/2_core_workflow.html)
- Exercise: [Planning a library prep](module2/exercises/2_planning.html)

## Module 3 — Application-specific libraries

RNA-seq, ChIP-seq / ATAC-seq, amplicon and single-cell libraries — what changes and why.

- Lecture: [Library types](module3/lectures/3_library_types.html)
- Exercise: [Choosing a library type](module3/exercises/3_choosing.html)

## Module 4 — Library QC, pooling and sequencing

Quantification, fragment-size analysis, multiplexing with indexes, and checking the reads that come back.

- Lecture: [QC and pooling](module4/lectures/4_qc_pooling.html)
- Exercise: [Pooling calculations](module4/exercises/4_pooling.html)
